topic: Tribes and Folk Traditions of Uttar Pradesh
description: Uttar Pradesh is a state rich in cultural diversity. It is home to various Scheduled Tribes (ST) and boasts a unique heritage of folk music, folk dances, and traditional fairs, which are crucial for the State Specific GK section.

sections.title: Geographical Distribution of Major Tribes
sections.description: The geographical spread and origin of major Scheduled Tribes residing in different districts of Uttar Pradesh.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Terai Region (Maharajganj, Siddharthnagar, Shravasti, Bahraich, Lakhimpur Kheri)
geographical_data.key_characteristics: The largest tribe in Uttar Pradesh. They belong to the Kirat Dynasty and possess distinct physical features.
They claim descent from the Patwar Rajput clan. The practices of hypergamy and hypogamy are prevalent within the tribe.
Originally migrated from the Palamu region of Jharkhand. They are known for their brave and martial nature.
Recognized as a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) predominantly residing in the Bundelkhand region.

sections.title: Cultural Characteristics of Tribes
sections.description: Unique traditions, festivals, and social systems specific to the tribes of UP.

key_concepts.explanation: A traditional festival celebrated by the Tharu tribe during the Hindu calendar months of Jyeshtha and Vaishakha.

key_concepts.concept: Diwali as a Festival of Sorrow
key_concepts.explanation: The Tharu tribe observes Diwali as a day of mourning rather than celebration, dedicating the day to remembering and offering food to their ancestors.
Goddess Chamunda is the primary deity of the Buksa tribe. They also have a deep reverence for the Peepal tree.
A traditional marriage custom prevalent in the Tharu tribe, which involves the mutual exchange of brides between two families.

sections.title: Major Folk Dances of Uttar Pradesh
sections.description: Prominent traditional dances associated with different cultural regions of the state.

key_associations.extra_info: Women perform this spectacular dance balancing a multi-tiered wooden pyramid featuring 108 lit earthen lamps on their heads. It symbolizes the birth of Goddess Radha.
A tribal dance primarily performed by the Kharwar tribe to invoke the blessings of the Karma deity for good fortune and a rich harvest.
Also known as the 'Peacock Dance', it is performed by women of the Bedia community, especially on the occasion of Krishna Janmashtami.
Performed by the Dhobi (washerman) community on auspicious occasions, beautifully depicting the emotional relationship between a washerman and his donkey.

sections.title: Major Folk Songs and Music
sections.description: Distinctive vocal styles that reflect the geographical and cultural nuances of UP.

key_associations.extra_info: A melodious folk song typically sung by women during the monsoon month of Shravan, expressing longing for the beloved.
Primarily sung by the Ahir community. It is rich in the themes of separation (Virah) and often includes heroic and historical tales.
A vigorous heroic ballad recounting the bravery, battles, and martial exploits of the legendary warrior brothers 'Alha and Udal' of Mahoba.
Folk songs exclusively based on the divine love stories, playful teasing, and pastimes of Lord Krishna and Goddess Radha.

sections.title: Major Fairs of Uttar Pradesh
sections.description: Historical, commercial, and religious fairs organized annually across the state.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: A grand fair that stands as a symbol of Hindu-Muslim unity, hosting both the Nauchandi Devi Temple and the shrine of the Sufi saint Bale Miyan.
Organized on the banks of the Yamuna River, it is the state's largest cattle and camel fair, known for its religious and commercial significance.
India's second-largest cattle fair, traditionally held on the auspicious occasion of Kartik Purnima.
A massive religious fair organized at the Shakumbhari Devi temple in the Shivalik foothills during the Navratri festival.

sections.title: Exam-Oriented Important Facts
sections.description: Direct, one-liner facts related to the tribes, arts, and culture of Uttar Pradesh.

important_facts.fact: Sonbhadra district possesses the highest Scheduled Tribe (ST) population in Uttar Pradesh.
Baghpat district has the lowest Scheduled Tribe (ST) population in the state.
Ayodhya and Jalaun are the only two districts in Uttar Pradesh that have absolutely zero Scheduled Tribe population.
In 1967, five tribes of Uttar Pradesh (Tharu, Buksa, Bhotia, Jaunsari, and Raji) were granted official Scheduled Tribe (ST) status for the first time.
Kathak is the only recognized Classical Dance form originating from Uttar Pradesh, with the Lucknow and Varanasi Gharanas being its most prominent centers.
